sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS utility_patent_count
FROM (
    SELECT p.patent_id
    FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p
    LEFT JOIN PATENTS.CITATIONS c
        ON c.cited_patent_id = p.patent_id
        AND c.cite_grant_date BETWEEN p.filing_date AND DATEADD(year, 10, p.filing_date)
    WHERE p.patent_type = 'Utility'
      AND EXTRACT(year FROM p.grant_date) = 2010
    GROUP BY p.patent_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.citing_patent_id) = 1
) AS filtered_patents;
reasoning: The query first filters PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS for utility patents granted in 2010. It then left‑joins to a forward citation table (PATENTS.CITATIONS) restricting citations to those whose grant date falls within ten years after the original patent's filing date. By grouping on the original patent ID and using HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.citing_patent_id) = 1, we keep only patents with exactly one qualifying forward citation. Finally, the outer SELECT counts the distinct patents that satisfy all conditions.
